newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Tsang says no fear of attack on HK currency.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tsang says no fear of attack on HK currency.

text.p: Hong Kong's Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said on Friday the territory could withstand speculative attacks on its dollar.
"We are confident in the ability of our exchange rate system to withstand shocks and speculative attacks," Tsang told a business function.
The Hong Kong dollar is pegged to the U.S. dollar at HK$7.80.

"We have a robust monetary regime that has time and again stood up well to abrupt developments. We have effective monetary devices which we have no hesitation to use when our linked exchange rate comes under unwarranted pressure," Tsang said.
"We have ample foreign exchange reserves for maintaining exchange rate stability. And our banking sector is in a healthy financial state and subject to appropriate supervision."
Hong Kong holds foreign currency reserves of about US$82 billion, the fifth largest in the world.
Tsang stressed that a "prudent budget and tight discipline in the management of public finances" were the key to weathering a currency crisis.

The Hong Kong dollar has been trading at a stable level of about HK$7.74 to the U.S. dollar, although currency forwards came under pressure earlier this week as speculators took positions and investors aggressively hedged theirs.
Several Asian currencies have been under speculative attack recently.
The Thai baht, Malaysian ringgit, Philippines peso and Indonesian rupiah have suffered de facto devaluations against the U.S. dollar due to the pressure.
Tsang also said Hong Kong's proposed pension scheme, the Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF), would be a strong boost to the territory's capital market.

"The substantial amount of savings institutionalised by an MPF scheme will create a huge new source of supply of long-term investment funds for our corporate sector to be moblised through long-term debt instruments," he said, adding that the debt market would become more active in the territory.
